cluster_summary: This cluster includes vulnerabilities in WebSocket, HTTP/2, and Socket.IO implementations where missing checks on message types, flags, sizes, and connection limits lead to resource exhaustion, memory disclosure, or denial of service. The root causes are assumptions about input structure and lack of bounds on resource consumption, requiring targeted validation and rate/connection/size limits.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata into memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work. Report code paths where protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work.

mechanism.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanism.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanism.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Count RST_STREAM frames per time window and close the connection with GO_AWAY when the count exceeds a threshold.
sub_patterns.name: Missing rate limiting on high-frequency control frames
sub_patterns.root_cause: The HTTP/2 implementation does not enforce a rate limit on RST_STREAM frames, allowing an attacker to rapidly cancel streams and exhaust server resources.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Set maxPayload on WebSocketServer constructor or server configuration to reject frames exceeding a configurable byte limit before processing.
sub_patterns.name: Missing maximum message/frame size limit
sub_patterns.root_cause: WebSocket server accepts messages without a maximum size limit, allowing an attacker to send oversized messages that consume unbounded memory and CPU.
